name: XBOW
description: Autonomous offensive security platform that uses AI to discover and validate software vulnerabilities at scale, replacing manual penetration testing.
threat: Autonomous AI pentesting commoditizes a core revenue stream for traditional MDR/EDR vendors and reduces dependence on human red teams that CRWD and PANW rely on as high-margin services.

name: Socket
description: Software supply chain security platform that protects enterprises from malicious open-source dependencies introduced via AI-assisted coding.
threat: Addresses the fastest-growing attack surface in enterprise security — AI-generated code pulling in unvetted open-source packages — where CRWD and ZS lack native depth.

name: Torq
description: Agentic AI security operations platform automating SOC workflows, alert triage, and incident response for multinational enterprises.
threat: Agentic SOC automation threatens the professional-services and Cortex XSOAR revenues of PANW and the Singularity suite upsell economics of SentinelOne.

name: Abnormal AI
description: AI-native email and collaboration security platform using behavioral analysis to stop sophisticated phishing, BEC, and account-takeover attacks.
threat: Behavioral AI email security erodes email gateway revenues at PANW and CRWD and competes directly with OKTA's identity-centric threat detection as BEC attacks evolve.

name: Zafran Security
description: AI-native threat exposure management platform that uses existing security tools to prove 90% of critical vulnerabilities are unexploitable and autonomously remediates the remaining 10%.
threat: Directly challenges vulnerability management modules in PANW's Cortex and CRWD's Falcon by reducing remediation times from weeks to hours using AI-native exposure scoring.

name: Zenity
description: Cybersecurity platform that governs and secures autonomous AI agents across enterprise environments, preventing agent-level attacks and data exfiltration.
threat: As enterprises deploy millions of AI agents, Zenity's AI-agent governance layer fills a gap that CRWD, OKTA, and ZS have not yet addressed natively, threatening to become the de facto control plane for agentic security.

name: Eye Security
description: European integrated cybersecurity platform combining AI-powered threat detection, 24/7 human SOC, incident response, and in-house cyber insurance for mid-market enterprises.
threat: Challenges FTNT and PANW's European mid-market position by offering a sovereign, GDPR-compliant integrated stack — particularly relevant as NIS2 drives mandatory security spend.

name: Isomorphic Labs
description: Alphabet-spun AI drug design company using AlphaFold-derived models to design novel therapeutics across multiple modalities, with partnerships with Lilly, Novartis, and J&J.
threat: If IsoDDE delivers clinical candidates at scale, Isomorphic becomes a platform layer that renders traditional CRO-based discovery at LLY and NVO obsolete and could capture royalties on drug programs at both companies.

name: Chai Discovery
description: AI molecular design company building foundation models that predict and reprogram molecular interactions for drug discovery, with pharma partnerships with Lilly, Pfizer, and Novartis.
threat: Chai-3's double-digit experimental success rate in de novo antibody design directly erodes SDGR's computational chemistry and RXRX's phenomics edge while commoditizing early discovery for big pharma partners LLY and NVO.

name: Xaira Therapeutics
description: Integrated AI biotech using generative protein design and large biological models to discover next-generation therapeutics targeting hard-to-drug biology.
threat: With the deepest capital base in AI-native drug discovery and Nobel laureate co-founder David Baker, Xaira threatens to bypass clinical-stage public biotechs like VRTX by generating first-in-class biologics that legacy platforms cannot reach.

name: EvolutionaryScale
description: AI protein language model company (ESM3) that generates novel proteins compressing millions of years of evolution, enabling therapeutic and industrial biotech applications.
threat: ESM3's open and commercial protein generation platform challenges ILMN's sequencing-centric data moat and SDGR's structural biology software by making de novo protein design accessible and cheap.

name: insitro
description: AI drug discovery company founded by Daphne Koller building a data engine around human biology with partnerships with BMS (ALS), Gilead (NASH), and Lilly (metabolism).
threat: insitro's Virtual Human platform competing on ALS, NASH, and metabolic targets with BMS and Lilly validation undermines the narrative that public TechBio companies like RXRX have a monopoly on AI-native discovery.

name: Genesis Therapeutics
description: AI-native drug discovery company focused on generative chemistry and translational biology to produce clinical-stage small molecules for undruggable targets.
threat: Genesis's generative chemistry platform directly competes with SDGR's Maestro and RXRX's Recursion OS by targeting the same undruggable protein space, threatening to make SDGR's software licensing model irrelevant.

name: Form Energy
description: Long-duration iron-air battery company capable of 100-hour discharge, targeting multi-day grid storage to complement intermittent renewables and AI data center power needs.
threat: Iron-air chemistry with 10x lower cost per kWh than lithium threatens FLNC's and EOSE's long-duration propositions and could undercut TSLA's Megapack pricing for utility-scale deployments.

name: Redwood Materials
description: Battery recycling and cathode production company founded by ex-Tesla CTO JB Straubel, now expanding into second-life EV battery energy storage for AI data centers.
threat: Redwood's recycling-to-cathode loop threatens ALB and MP by creating a domestic circular supply chain that reduces dependence on virgin lithium and rare earth imports, potentially capping long-term lithium pricing power.

name: Base Power
description: Residential and commercial energy storage company offering a 39.2 kWh home battery (Core) with 36-hour backup, deploying as a virtual power plant network.
threat: Base Power's $13B valuation and VPP network model directly challenges ENPH's IQ Battery dominance and TSLA's Powerwall by offering longer backup duration and a utility-facing fleet monetization layer.

name: Sila Nanotechnologies
description: Battery materials startup producing silicon-carbon anode material that increases energy density for EVs and grid storage, with manufacturing in Moses Lake, WA.
threat: Silicon-carbon anodes that replace graphite threaten ALB's and MP's position in the battery materials supply chain by reducing lithium requirements per kWh and enabling denser packs that close Tesla's range advantage.

name: Mariana Minerals
description: Software-first vertically integrated critical minerals company using MarianaOS to autonomously operate copper and lithium mines in Utah and Texas.
threat: Autonomous mining operations targeting 50,000 MT/yr copper and first GWh-scale lithium-from-produced-water facility directly threatens MP's rare earth and ALB's lithium market positions with domestically sourced supply.

name: CMBlu Energy
description: German non-lithium battery maker with SolidFlow organic redox technology offering 10+ hour storage without lithium, cobalt, or nickel, with supply agreements with Uniper.
threat: FEOC-compliant non-lithium chemistry with 5 GWh Uniper supply agreement threatens FLNC's and EOSE's market positioning by offering a regulatory-advantaged, critical-mineral-free alternative for European grid storage.

name: Stripe
description: Global payments infrastructure platform processing $1.9T annually, expanding into stablecoins (Bridge), programmable wallets (Privy), and a blockchain for payments (Tempo).
threat: Stripe's $1.9T payment volume and stablecoin/blockchain expansion (Bridge, Tempo) directly challenges V and MA's network fees and positions Stripe as the infrastructure layer for next-generation AI-agent-initiated payments.

name: Revolut
description: UK-based global neobank with 70M+ customers, full banking licenses in UK, EU, Mexico, and Australia, offering payments, crypto, insurance, and business banking.
threat: Revolut's $115B valuation, full banking licenses across 4 jurisdictions, and pending US bank charter threaten PYPL's global digital wallet dominance and V/MA's cross-border fee revenue as it builds a full-stack bank.

name: Ramp
description: AI-powered financial operations platform for corporates covering spend management, corporate cards, procurement, accounting, and AI token spend optimization with $1B+ ARR.
threat: Ramp's corporate card and AI spend management at $44B valuation competes directly with V and MA's commercial card interchange revenue and threatens PYPL's B2B push by automating the entire corporate payment workflow.

name: Figure AI
description: Humanoid robotics company building AI-powered general-purpose robots for commercial and residential deployment, already deployed at BMW manufacturing plants.
threat: Figure's humanoid robots automating labor-intensive workflows threaten fintech-adjacent infrastructure companies like Block/XYZ that depend on human-operated retail and point-of-sale ecosystems.

name: Iambic Therapeutics
description: AI drug discovery company using Enchant platform for translational prediction and generative chemistry to produce clinical-stage small molecules.
threat: Iambic's translational prediction platform targets the same hard-to-drug small molecule space as SDGR, potentially delivering clinical candidates faster and undercutting SDGR's commercial discovery partnerships.

name: Anthropic
description: AI safety company building Claude large language models with industry-leading enterprise penetration through Claude Code (coding), Cowork (agents), and API integrations.
threat: Claude Code's viral adoption and Cowork agent platform threaten MSFT's GitHub Copilot monetization, CRM's Agentforce, and NOW's AI-workflow products by offering a model-layer alternative that bypasses incumbent vendor lock-in.

name: OpenAI
description: Developer of GPT and o-series foundation models powering ChatGPT, Codex, and enterprise APIs, with $110B raised and strategic cloud partnerships with Amazon, NVIDIA, and SoftBank.
threat: OpenAI's Codex and enterprise APIs are embedding at the model layer of MSFT's Azure stack while also competing with MSFT's own Copilot products, creating internal conflicts that threaten CRM, NOW, and SNOW customer relationships.

name: Databricks
description: Data intelligence and AI platform (Lakehouse, Lakebase, Agent Bricks) enabling enterprises to build AI apps and agents on proprietary data, with $1.5B+ Lakebase ARR.
threat: Databricks at $190B has already surpassed SNOW in private market value and its Lakebase-plus-Agent Bricks stack directly displaces SNOW's data cloud and MDB's Atlas for AI-native enterprise workloads.

name: Cognition (Devin)
description: Autonomous AI software engineer (Devin) with $492M ARR and 50% MoM growth serving enterprises including NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Mercedes-Benz.
threat: Devin's autonomous coding with $492M ARR threatens MSFT's GitHub Copilot Enterprise pricing and CRM's developer tools by offering a full-cycle autonomous engineering agent that replaces workflow automation modules.

name: Cohere
description: Enterprise-focused LLM platform (Command, Embed, Rerank) built for secure, private on-premise and cloud deployments with partnerships with Oracle, SAP, Dell, and government agencies.
threat: Cohere's enterprise-grade, air-gapped LLM deployment model challenges MSFT's Azure OpenAI exclusivity and GOOGL's Vertex AI by giving regulated industries (finance, defense, government) a sovereign AI option without cloud hyperscaler dependency.

name: Bridge (Stripe subsidiary)
description: Stablecoin orchestration platform acquired by Stripe for $1.1B, processing $400B+ in stablecoin B2B payments annually and expanding Stripe's crypto payment rails globally.
threat: Bridge's $400B stablecoin volume flowing through Stripe's infrastructure threatens COIN's and CRCL's stablecoin payment ambitions by embedding crypto rails into a $159B payments incumbent that already serves 1.6% of global GDP.

name: Inforcer
description: MSP-focused Microsoft 365 security management platform with Shadow AI detection and real-time threat response, serving SMB clients through managed service providers.
threat: Inforcer's Shadow AI detection and 300% YoY growth in the underserved SMB/MSP market threatens OKTA's identity management and CRWD's Falcon Go product by offering an all-in-one Microsoft 365 security stack at a fraction of the cost.

name: Writer
description: Enterprise generative AI platform for deploying AI agents across business workflows including content creation, customer support, and knowledge management with full data governance.
threat: Writer's enterprise AI agent workflows with Fortune 500 customers like Vanguard and L'Oreal directly compete with CRM's Agentforce and NOW's AI workflow modules by offering model-agnostic agentic automation at lower total cost.

name: Neon (Databricks subsidiary)
description: Serverless Postgres database platform designed for AI agents, enabling instant spin-up of isolated database environments for agentic coding workflows (acquired by Databricks for $1B).
threat: Neon's Lakebase integration into Databricks' Agent Bricks creates a purpose-built agentic database stack that threatens MDB's Atlas and SNOW's Cortex as the default data substrate for AI agent workloads.

name: Klarna
description: Swedish buy-now-pay-later pioneer with 85M+ consumers globally, AI-driven underwriting, and a fully automated customer service model targeting V/MA merchant fees.
threat: Klarna's AI-automated underwriting and checkout network serving 85M consumers directly threatens AFRM's US market share and erodes V/MA merchant discount rates by routing BNPL transactions off traditional card rails.
